title: TypeScript SDK: structured-output helpers, discriminated unions, and Zod/JSON-Schema generator
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: TypeScript users building apps with structured model outputs (e.g., JSON objects, typed tool responses) need ergonomic runtime validation, compile-time types, and predictable behavior for streaming responses and retries. Current TS SDK surface has ad-hoc helpers and several community requests for: 1) automatic type generation from declared response shapes, 2) first-class support for discriminated unions (tagged unions) from model outputs, 3) Zod and JSON-Schema helpers that integrate with streaming parsers, and 4) clear retry semantics when a streaming parse fails mid-response.

Goal: Ship a TypeScript SDK feature set that: (A) accepts a developer-facing schema (Zod or JSON-Schema) or an inline TypeScript type and produces runtime validators and compile-time types, (B) supports discriminated unions with a minimal runtime (tag-based dispatch), (C) provides robust streaming ergonomics (incremental parse APIs, backpressure, and a safe resume/retry story), and (D) includes examples and docs for common patterns (tool calling, function chaining, and failed-parse recovery).
acceptance_criteria: ts-sdk exposes a new createStructuredParser(schema) API that returns: parseStream(stream): AsyncIterable<Either<ValidatedObject, ParseError>> and parse(text): Result<T>
Codegen CLI (rn: redwood-ts-typegen) converts a Zod or JSON-Schema input into TypeScript types + runtime zod validators and emits a small helper for discriminated unions
Discriminated union helpers support single-field tags (e.g., { kind: 'tool' | 'message' }) and nested tag mapping and are covered by unit tests (>= 90% coverage for helpers)

Streaming parse supports graceful failure: when a chunk causes a schema validation error, SDK emits a ParseError with offset and original text and surface a retry token to allow resume from the last-good-offset

Examples folder in repo with 3 scenarios: (1) function-calling response typed with Zod, (2) multi-part streaming assistant response with partial objects, (3) retry-after-parse-failure using resume token
Docs page in Console and README with code snippets for zod and json-schema workflows
No breaking changes to existing TS SDK public methods (backwards compatible).
decisions: Primary runtime validator: Zod. Rationale: developer ergonomics, popularity, small bundle for tree-shaking. JSON-Schema supported as a secondary input path via conversion (ajv -> zod conversion shim).
Discriminant field default: 'type' but API allows custom tag key via options. Keep runtime cost low by compiling a small dispatch map at initialization.

Streaming parser approach: prefer incremental JSON tokenizer + zod-safe-parse on completed objects rather than attempting streaming zod validation. This minimizes per-token validation work and simplifies error/rerun handling.

Retry semantics: SDK will surface a resume token (opaque string) when a parse error occurs mid-stream. The token encodes lastGoodByteOffset + modelRequestId + schemaVersion. Resume is best-effort — document that model non-determinism may still cause different content after retry.

Codegen UX: standalone CLI (redwood-codegen) with an option --runtime=zod or --runtime=ajv that outputs a .ts file with types and runtime validators. The CLI will be shipped in the monorepo under packages/codegen.

comments: 2025-01-21: Priya Shah - Kicked off RFC draft in /docs/rfcs/ts-structured-output.md. Initial proposal includes API sketches for createStructuredParser and basic codegen outline.

2025-01-24: Liam Chen - Prototype of streaming tokenizer committed to feature/stream-parser branch. Tokenizer finds JSON object boundaries in chunked assistant streams. Missing zod wiring and resume token design.

2025-01-28: Maria Alvarez (Design review) - Suggests UX for error messages: include snippet and a one-click copy to retry with resume token in Console examples. Also wants example for nested discriminants (e.g., { kind: 'tool', tool: { name: 'search', result: {...} } }).

2025-01-30: Samir Patel (Security) - Reviewed resume token idea. Proposed HMAC using request id + secret in server-side code to avoid token forgery. Marked security_review_required = true for final design. Currently flagged for follow-up.

2025-02-02: Liam Chen - Added unit tests for discriminated-union helper (pass) and an integration test that simulates mid-stream truncation (asserts resume token returned). Found an edge-case where whitespace-only chunks cause delayed boundary detection; added fix in tokenizer.
2025-02-03: Priya Shah - Updated acceptance criteria to require docs and examples. Created docs issue PM-412 to coordinate examples and Console writeup.
related_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/1355 - feat: zod helpers and discriminant utils
notes: Keep public API stable: default to Zod but accept raw TS types via `as const` codegen output. We will stage JSON-Schema as secondary input to avoid forked maintenance paths. Plan for Go/Python parity in next cycle; create language-agnostic resume token format.
